top_stories.title: A leak reveals that Anthropic is testing a more capable AI model "Claude Mythos"
top_stories.summary: A data leak has revealed that Anthropic is internally testing a new, more powerful AI model called Claude Mythos. The company has described it as representing a 'step change in capabilities' beyond its current model lineup. The leak provides a rare glimpse into Anthropic's upcoming model pipeline ahead of any official announcement.

top_stories.title: Judge sides with Anthropic to temporarily block the Pentagon's ban
top_stories.summary: A judge has issued a temporary injunction blocking the Pentagon from enforcing a supply-chain risk designation against Anthropic, which had threatened the company's ability to do business with the US government. The ruling is a significant legal win for Anthropic, which had challenged the designation in court. The case highlights growing tensions between AI companies and national security agencies over procurement and risk classification.

top_stories.title: Google is making it easier to import another AI's memory into Gemini
top_stories.summary: Google is introducing a feature that allows users to import conversation history and memory from other AI assistants directly into Gemini. The move is designed to reduce friction for users switching from rival AI products and make Gemini more personalised from the outset. It signals an increasingly competitive battle among AI assistants for user lock-in through memory and personalisation features.

top_stories.title: I Asked ChatGPT 500 Questions. Here Are the Ads I Saw Most Often
top_stories.summary: Wired conducted a systematic investigation into ChatGPT's advertising behaviour, asking 500 questions to catalogue which ads appeared and how frequently. The experiment sheds light on how OpenAI is monetising its flagship chatbot through sponsored content and what categories of advertisers are prioritising the platform. The findings offer early consumer research into AI-native advertising patterns.

top_stories.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated articles
top_stories.summary: Wikipedia has introduced a policy banning the use of AI-generated content in articles, citing concerns about accuracy, sourcing, and the integrity of the encyclopaedia's volunteer-driven model. The decision reflects broader debates in academic and publishing communities about the appropriate role of generative AI in producing authoritative text. The ban applies to article content but the full scope of the policy is still being clarified.

further_links.title: David Sacks is no longer the White House AI and Crypto Czar
further_links.summary: David Sacks has stepped down from his role as the White House's AI and Crypto Czar, ending his tenure overseeing the administration's technology policy agenda.

further_links.title: Google's 'live' AI search assistant can handle conversations in dozens more languages
further_links.summary: Google has expanded its live AI search assistant to support dozens of additional languages, broadening access to conversational AI-powered search globally.

further_links.title: Apple will reportedly allow other AI chatbots to plug into Siri
further_links.summary: Apple is reportedly planning to open Siri to third-party AI chatbot integrations as part of an upcoming iOS update, potentially allowing rivals like ChatGPT deeper system-level access.

further_links.title: STADLER reshapes knowledge work at a 230-year-old company
further_links.summary: OpenAI's blog profiles how STADLER, a rail vehicle manufacturer with over two centuries of history, has deployed AI tools to transform knowledge management and internal workflows.

further_links.title: New York City hospitals drop Palantir as controversial AI firm expands in UK
further_links.summary: New York City's public hospital system has ended its contract with Palantir while the data analytics company simultaneously expands its AI healthcare operations in the United Kingdom.

further_links.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live: Making audio AI more natural and reliable
further_links.summary: Google DeepMind has published a blog post detailing improvements to Gemini's live audio capabilities, focusing on more natural-sounding, lower-latency conversational AI interactions.

further_links.title: Meet the Tech Reporters Using AI to Help Write and Edit Their Stories
further_links.summary: Wired examines how journalists at technology publications are increasingly using AI tools to assist with drafting, editing, and researching their reporting.

further_links.title: AI Research Is Getting Harder to Separate From Geopolitics
further_links.summary: Wired reports that AI research produced in China is increasingly being viewed through a geopolitical lens, with international collaboration and publication becoming more fraught as tensions between the US and China deepen.

further_links.title: AI got the blame for the Iran school bombing. The truth is more worrying
further_links.summary: The Guardian investigates claims that AI was responsible for targeting decisions in the Iran school bombing, finding the reality of how military and intelligence systems operate is more complex and troubling than the AI narrative suggested.

further_links.title: School uses AI to remove 200 books, including Orwell's 1984 and Twilight
further_links.summary: A school has used an AI tool to review and remove over 200 books from its library, including classic titles like George Orwell's 1984, prompting concern from librarians and educators about AI-driven censorship.
